messages.subject: Getting Results from RBroker
parts:
I recently tried to do some calculations using the RBroker API for .NET.  Here is the scenario that I am faced with:
1. I will be passed an RScript with n-many input variables and n-many output variables
2. I will be passed a collection of input variables to map to the script
3. I will be passed a collection of output variable names to look values up for when the script has completed successfully.
4. return all output variables, plots, console, etc... back to the caller.

In DeployR, this is fairly straight forward, but with RBroker, I am unable to determine where to get this information.  I looked in the RTaskResult class and it doesn't appear to be there.  The exact same R-Script and variables are working as expected in DeployR, but not RBroker.

I used the sample Background example, creating BackgroundTaskOptions, a BackgroundTaskListener and even the RBorkerStatsHelper class to try and capture the results from the Task submission, but no luck thus far.  There has to be a way to pull back the output variables after submitting a Task using RBroker, right?

Thanks,

Scott

messages.author: 1eafd5d24fb29c12
messages.subject: Re: Getting Results from RBroker
parts:
Hi Scott,

A Background RBroker task, creates a DeployR Job, that runs asynchronously.  When the Job has completed, the results are store in a Project that is persisted to the repository.  So, you have 2 options.   Get a handle to the project and retrieve the results (some sample code shown below), or run your Script as a Discrete RBroker task

To get the project created by a job from a Background RBroker task

  //get the job id
  String jobID = rTaskResult.getID(); 
  //get a reference to the Authenticated user
  RUser rUser = m_rBroker.owner();
  //get a reference to the DeployR job
  RJob rJob = rUser.queryJob(jobID);
  // make sure we have a valid project id
  if (rJob.query().project.Length > 0)
  {
      //get the project using the project id
       RProject rProject = rUser.getProject(rJob.query().project);

      //now call listObjects, listFiles, listResults on the project
  }

messages.author: d45f5f779ca93eee
messages.subject: Re: Getting Results from RBroker
parts:
Hi Scott,

The code snippet provided above by David C. correctly explains how you would retrieve your task results when working with the Background task runtime. What follows here is more general advice on working with the framework and also a recommendation.

Your initial intuition to look for your task output variables, plots, console, etc. in the RTaskResult was absolutely correct. In most cases, those data would indeed be available on the RTaskResult. However, when working with the Background task runtime specifically, things work a little bit differently. This is because the Background task runtime is intended to be used when you anticipate long-running tasks that you would like to schedule for execution now and then have your application collect the results at some future date, perhaps hours or days later.

Based on the description you provided of your own use case it sounds like you want to execute your tasks and collect the results immediately. If that is the case, then the Background task runtime is probably not the right choice. You should consider using the Discrete task runtime or if maximizing throughput is very important to you, perhaps the Pooled task runtime. Using either the Discrete or Pooled task runtime your task results will be directly available to your application in your RTaskResults.

If you haven't had a chance to do so, I recommend checking out the RBroker Framework tutorial. It provides a step-by-step introduction to the framework. Importantly, the RBroker Runtime Options section discusses the suitability of each supported runtime which is definitely worth looking over. At the end of the day, choosing the right runtime is key to getting the most from the framework, while keeping things simple in your application code.

David R

messages.author: 1eafd5d24fb29c12
messages.subject: Re: Getting Results from RBroker
parts:
Hi Scott,

Using an RScript via a Discrete Task is easy.  In the example below we are executing the "DeployR - Hello World" RScript, owned by user "testuser" in directory "root" in the DeployR Repository.   We are passing a numeric value to the "input_randomNum" R object as an input to the script, and we are requesting R object "x" as an output.   

The big advantage of using the RBroker Framework is that you have 3 simple steps to follow:  define your RTask, submit the RTask, and retrieve the results using RTaskResult.   The RBroker handles the queuing of the task, execution, error handling,etc.  It is especially powerful for applications that require high throughput and pools of R sessions.   It is built on top of the DeployR Client Library.  If you feel more comfortable using the DeployR Client Library, that is perfectly fine. 


               DiscreteTaskOptions options = new DiscreteTaskOptions();
                //specify the inputs to the script
                options.rinputs.Add(RDataFactory.createNumeric("input_randomNum", 100));
                //tell the broker which R objects we want to return
                options.routputs.Add("x");

                RTask rTask = RTaskFactory.discreteTask("DeployR - Hello World",
                                                                "root",
                                                                "testuser",
                                                                "",
                                                                options);
